notes.title: Co-Op Career Mode Beta is LIVE!
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45193365/3a90c27ca386dffe99e55578aca9f81ec1b3a604.png"]⚠️ Important Notes Before You Join
This is a beta build → expect bugs, rough edges, and unpredictable behaviour. 

There is always a chance this build could cause issues with your save data (career progress). 

As a precaution, please back up your save files before playing.
 👉 Full, step by step instructions on how to do this are posted in a pinned discussion on the Steam Community Hub (link below).


How to Join the Beta[olist]
Make sure you are not running Spray Paint Simulator.

Go to your Steam Library, right click Spray Paint Simulator and choose Properties 

Select the Betas tab 

Under Private Betas, enter the access code:
 BetaTestBranch → click Check Code 

From the dropdown, choose:  betatest - Beta Test Branch 

Steam will update the game and you will be ready to test
[/olist]
If you have successfully switched to the beta test, you should see 'Co-Op Career Mode Beta Test' displayed on the main menu of the game when you launch it.

  
How to Go Back to the Standard Game
Open the Betas tab again 

From the dropdown, select:
 None (leave all beta programs) 

Steam will update the game back to the regular version 
Feedback and Bug Reports
Please share your feedback and any bug reports in the pinned discussion thread. Keeping everything in one place helps us stay organised.

👉 https://steamcommunity.com/app/1811340/discussions/0/604166720297492033/

We cannot wait to see what you all think. Thanks for testing this with us.
 — Adam and Nick

notes.title: Improved Scaffolding
notes.content:
It's now easier to get on/off scaffolding ladders and it is also slightly taller.
 Invert look now also applies to aim mode.
 Battery placement now resets when reloading the level (in case you've lost the battery somewhere)

notes.title: Improved task highlighter and cherry picker
notes.content:
Task highlight for unpainted areas has been extended to consider neighbouring pixels making areas of low paint density show up better.
 The cherry picker has a number of automatic stability improvements
 A few beams on the bridge have slightly lower paint requirements to better account for the use of the medium nozzle.
 Save on termination now explicitly ensures it is never asynchronous

notes.title: Moved floating cash, improved robot, neater ending
notes.content:
A cash pile was left floating in mid air after some bridge beams were removed, this has been fixed.
 The paint required for the center chest panel on the robot has been reduced as some people found it difficult.
 The message at the end of career mode has been changed and it now shows the credits.

notes.title: Improved Cherry Picker
notes.content:
Some general improvements to the behaviour and stability of the Cherry Picker


 Better collision detection when raising and lowering the arm.
 Better automatic braking around the large robot.

notes.title: Difficulty setting, very large scaffolding
notes.content:
New extra large scaffolding.
 Trimmed down bridge job, removed some beams.
 Difficulty slider in the options allows reducing difficulty if stuck.
 Option to turn off timelapse capture - potential fix for skipping mouse.
 Improved Cherry Picker, gets stuck less easily, fixed camera jump when getting off.
 Prevented picking up and moving items when on the Cherry Picker
 Improved item placement from the store

notes.title: Improvements to the Cherry Picker and Yopaint 3000
notes.content:
Cherry picker overhead camera 
 Cherry picker tutorial message
 Yopaint 3000 increased range
 Yopiant 3000 tutorial message


A new overhead camera helps manoeuvring the cherry picker into position. Increased range of the Yopaint 3000 helps spray areas without extensions. 
 
These changes are aimed at improving the bridge level but should also help with the robot.

Some additional tutorial messages have been added to help players select the right equipment.

notes.title: Bigger scaffolding, better cherry picker
notes.content:
Latest fixes & improvements;


 Big scaffolding is one level higher, making the cherry picker optional
 Improved cherry picker physics, better driving stability
 Improved Nozzles, less likely to get stuck on the last few % 
 When focussed, spray tool range increases
 Small steps now work on scaffolding
 Paint tin capacity increased
 Paint usage rate reduced
 Prevented spray tool instantly spraying when it appears

notes.title: New Steam Update Available — What’s Coming Up
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

We wanted to send a special thank you to everyone who has played Spray Paint Simulator since its launch last Thursday. We have been blown away by the support and thoughtful feedback you have shared with us. It means a lot to our tiny team to see so many of you jumping in and giving the game a go!

Through your feedback, we have identified some issues and are working diligently to address them. While we are still working on a few things, we have recently rolled out a few fixes in the latest update:

 Scaffolding not unlocking after the Bus fix
 Reduced paper/tape usage rate
 Some balancing fixes to the large nozzle's paint usage
 Improved medium nozzle for Sprayite 150 & Yopaint 3000
 Cash pick-ups are available in other game modes
 Autosave every 5 minutes
 Climbing boots fixed
 Fixed a bug swapping spray tools between passes

You can check to see if you have updated to the most current version by checking to see if you're playing Build ID 18677495.

We have also added some additional launch options. The supported options are now: 


difficulty=4

Values of 0-5 are supported with 0 being the easiest and 5 being the game default


60fps

This should limit the framerate to a maximum of 60fps

 notimelapse

This switches off the timelapse capture of your progress. If you are struggling with mouse jumps or frame glitches this might help sort it out.

The launch options are only really intended to be quick fixes. We'll work on implementing more robust solutions ASAP, launch options just allow us to get solutions to you much more quickly.

What we have coming up

As we mentioned, there are still a few bug fixes that we’re working on which at the moment, are our top priority, but we also wanted to mention a few things we have in the forks for future updates. 

Co-Op Multiplayer in Career Mode

We are happy to see that so many people are eager to play with friends in Career Mode. As a small team, we had to make some difficult decisions to make sure we provided a solid game at launch, and we wanted to makes sure that we did have some kind of multiplayer available since we know how much fun getting creative with friends can be. But we know this is only the beginning. Expanding co-op is one of our top priorities and we plan on improving it in future updates.

The Cherry Picker

We’re glad that many people are enjoying this feature in the game, but realize that some improvements can be made. We are working on some that will enhance the experience, but these changes will take a little time to implement. So, please look forward to those in future updates.

Once again, we truly appreciate everyone who has taken the time to play and provide us with feedback. We are overwhelmed with the reception and we couldn’t be more grateful to you all!

If you have spotted anything or have suggestions, we would love to continute to hear from you. To make sure that nothing is missed, please feel free to submit any bugs or feedback to these forms:

 Bug Report
 Feedback

With more things to come, be sure to drop the game a follow to keep up to date with the latest announcements! You can also follow us on Twitter, Instagram,TikTok, and Discord, and check out our official website. 

Happy painting!
- Nick & Adam

notes.title: Spray Paint Simulator is Out Now!
notes.content:
Hello friends!

We are absolutely thrilled to share that our game, Spray Paint Simulator, is out now on Steam! 

[previewyoutube=0GVAf5pT0QQ;full][/previewyoutube] 

It’s been a long journey from forming our studio, to the initial idea for Spray Paint Simulator, and now, its release, and we couldn’t be more proud. After months of creating a game that we had loads of fun making, we’re very excited to be able to share it with the world. 

In the past, we’ve always made games for other people, so creating something ourselves has been both exciting and a little scary. When you launch a title, there’s always a mixture of sheer joy and nerves after putting it out there. We’re grateful for the support from our publisher and the many players who have helped us shape the game into something we’re eager for people to play. We’ve done our best to listen to player feedback and create a game we hope will be enjoyed by many. We can’t wait to see what players come up with during their time with the game. We hope you enjoy it!

As a thank you to the community, you can purchase Spray Paint Simulator at a 10% discount on Steam until June 4. 

We have lots in store for the future of Spray Paint Simulator, and always, we welcome your feedback, which you are welcome to share by filling out our feedback form. And if you happen to find a bug while you’re playing, you can quickly let us know here.  

With more things to come, be sure to drop the game a follow to keep up to date with the latest announcements! You can also follow us on Twitter, Instagram,TikTok, and Discord, and check out our official website. 

Happy painting!
- Nick & Adam

Hello friends!

We’re back again with a little more insight into what you’ll get to experience in Spray Paint Simulator when it launches this May! Today, we’d like to introduce you to one of the most unique jobs you’ll get to take on during your journey to become the best painter Spatterville has ever seen — a giant robot!

Yes, you read that correctly — you’ll get to paint a giant robot!

Tech genius and eccentric billionaire inventor, Zach, has finally achieved the unthinkable — his very own giant robot! While the design itself is a brilliant masterpiece, Zach needs your painting expertise to bring his vision to fruition. However, this is a massive job, so you’ll need to bring all the right tools with you (such as a recently restored cherry picker, perhaps?) and utilize all the techniques you’ve learned throughout your career. With a fresh coat of paint, the gargantuan ZACH-BOT 1 will be perfect, PERFECT! All that’s left is for the genius inventor to figure out just what to do with it…

notes.title: First Demo for Spray Paint Simulator Live Now
notes.content:
Hello friends!

We’re very excited to share that the first demo for Spray Paint Simulator is now available for you to play! We also revealed a new trailer during The MIX Fall Showcase — in case you missed it, you can watch it below:

[previewyoutube=K7PbnQQTLNA;full][/previewyoutube]
During the demo, you’ll be given your first job at the start of your career to become the best painter the town of Spatterville has ever seen! Start by purchasing your supplies, prepping the area, selecting the client’s desired colour, and then painting to perfection! Finally, remove the tape and paper for a satisfying reveal of a job well done! And don’t forget to grab your radio — a job isn’t any fun without some tunes! And if you colour outside the lines a bit, that’s no problem — the people of Spatterville are quite forgiving if there’s a little extra paint on the ground, or the grass, or their house… As progress won't be saved during this first demo, a little mess made here and there won't be of any matter!

But if you really want to get wild, then you’re in for a treat — check out Free Spray mode during the demo! With an array of lovely colours unlocked, you can create a rainbow world and paint anything you can reach! If you want a break, go exploring through the area — on foot or with the help of some scaffolding and ladders — to uncover some fun hidden secrets. 

We want to hear from you!

We want to make sure that Spray Paint Simulator is the best that it can be when it launches next year, so your feedback is invaluable. Once you’ve had a chance to try the demo, you are welcome to share your feedback with us by filling out our feedback form. And if you happen to find a bug while you’re playing, you can quickly let us know here. 

CARtwork Contest!

To celebrate the release of the demo, we thought it would be fun to hold a little artwork competition, as we would love to see the creativity you unleash while you play. 

To enter:

 Share a screenshot of your painted car from the demo and tag @northstarvg and @whitethorngames on Twitter, Bluesky, or Instagram OR via the Whitethorn Games Spray Paint Simulator channel on Discord
 Let your creativity shine, but please, no NSFW content, we’re family-friendly here
 Enter as many times as you like between November 21-December 6
 Winners will be announced on December 9 and will receive a code for the game!

Good luck, and may the best CARtwork win!

We’re thrilled to share Spray Paint Simulator and we hope you enjoy your time with the demo! We have a lot more in store for you over the next few months, so please make sure to drop the game a wishlist. You can also follow us on Twitter, Instagram,TikTok, and Discord, and check out our official website.
